text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--The government is prepared to give tax breaks totalling 500 million crowns to the sellers of companies bought by asset-strippers, if they voluntarily pay two billion crowns in state funds missed though the companies' break up.
--A record 65,000 people jammed the Tivoli amusement gardens to hear guitar legend Eric Clapton play in the five-member "Legends" jazz-blues band.
--Danish consumers are joining German, Italian and British conterparts in a trial of genetically engineered yoghurt and beer.
--Venture capital funds are doing well. DV Industri's equity grew by 99 percent last year and Dansk Kapitalanlaeg grew 66 percent.
--Burmeister & Wain Scandinavian Contractors have won a 620 million crown order to build a power station on the pacific island of Guam.
--A rise of between 30,000 and 40,000 children seeking nursery and childminding facilities was the main reason for local authority overspending last year.
--Mortgage companies are steadily taking more of the traditional retail loan market from banks, who are concentrating more on business customers.
